column1: # POLARIS key registry — every ops/CONVENTIONS.md key the kit reads, as DATA.
# TAB-separated: key<TAB>since<TAB>default<TAB>absent-cost<TAB>ask<TAB>scope      ('#' lines and blank lines ignored)
#   key          the CONVENTIONS.md header key, spelled exactly as `cfg` reads it
#   since        the kit version that introduced it
#   default      the EFFECTIVE value when the key is ABSENT — what the repo already behaves as, not
#                what INIT happens to write. For the three autonomy knobs these are the 6.0 values
#                (ops/contracts/hands-free-knobs.md v2), NOT the pre-6.0 ones. A `<placeholder>`
#                means there is no effective value: the key is optional, unset does nothing, and the
#                placeholder is what a human types in its place.
#   absent-cost  one plain-English line — what the repo loses, or behaves as, while the key is unset
#                interview asks it when the key is neither live nor stubbed (polaris interview); the
#                FIRST option is the default it pre-selects. `|`, `=` and TAB never appear inside a
#                question or a label. Empty on every row that is not one of the three interview keys.
#   scope        column 6 (6.21.0) — where a value may come from (ops/contracts/machine-prefs.md § 2):
#                machine = this repo's line, else this computer's preferences file, else the default ·
#                seed = INIT copies the machine value into a new repo, never read live · repo = this
#                repo's ops/CONVENTIONS.md only. Every row carries it, so a row with no question keeps
#                an EMPTY column 5 (`$5 == ""` still means "no question"). cfg's allowlist literal
#                (kit/ops/lib/core.sh) names exactly the `machine` rows — golden cfg-layers ties the two.
# Rows DOCUMENT; they never execute. Adding a row is data, not behavior. `polaris doctor` reports
# which of these an installed CONVENTIONS.md lacks, and `polaris adopt` appends one commented stub
# per absent key. Contract: ops/contracts/key-registry.md. ORDER IS MEANINGFUL — doctor names the
# first six absent keys in the order they appear below.

column4: the Planner offers Builder panes once; wt opens them for you, off only prints kickoffs
a work request runs the whole loop in one chat; panes stops the conductor after planning
big or risky tasks, planning and landing run on Opus; name another model to change it, or inherit to use the chat's own
ordinary tasks run on Opus; name another model to change it, or inherit to use the chat's own
small tasks run on Sonnet; name another model to change it, or inherit to use the chat's own
big or risky tasks run at high effort, never above the chat's own; inherit uses the chat's own effort
ordinary tasks run at medium effort, never above the chat's own; inherit uses the chat's own effort
small tasks run at low effort, never above the chat's own; inherit uses the chat's own effort
unset composes the hands-free trio since 6.0; autonomy: standard is the one-line opt-out
unset proceeds past a clean plan since 6.0; confirm waits for your go every time
unset lets Builders default reversible spec details since 6.0; ask returns every question
unset lets EVOLVE apply its inert allowlist since 6.0; confirm queues every item for approval
a run stops after the approved plan's own tasks; queue and backlog reach further
caps planner-promotion rounds under drain: backlog — ignored under any other drain mode
a run builds at most 12 tasks, then integrates what landed and reports (plan work is not counted)
a run takes no new work 90 minutes after kickoff — checked at wave boundaries only (plan work is not counted)
a run spawns at most 20 subagents in total, or 2 x its plan tasks if more (plan work is not counted)
the Check phase retries a red suite at most twice before handing you the failures
the runtime QA scout spawns only when uat: is empty AND the run touched a runnable: path
this repo declares no runnable surface, so qa_scout: auto resolves to off
no fast tier runs per handoff: a Builder runs only its card's own verify: checks, and the whole test: suite runs once per wave — set this to add a quick check to every handoff
every change runs the whole test: suite — set a template whose {tests} becomes the matched rows' tests globs, then map surfaces (surface: on tasks) to run only what a change can break

a docs/text-only change already skips the suite outright under this default; a value replaces the glob list (+ <globs> extends it instead) if your repo's doc/text paths differ, or set `-` to skip none

a change confined to a package whose test script is vitest or jest (runner installed), or to python files a pytest test reaches (the repo's own pytest command, narrowed to the related test files; node and python together run both), runs only the tests the runner itself relates to the changed files; set `-` to turn that off (node and python) and run the whole suite (or the SURFACES-selected subset) instead

a style, image or font-only change already runs the lighter look depth under this default (same visual: + --saw capture, no suite key); a value replaces the glob list (+ <globs> extends it instead) if other file types should count as look-only

a small component or page edit in a 1-2 point task already runs lint + typecheck + a look under this default, no suite (only where lint:/typecheck: or visual:+shot: are set); a value replaces the glob list (+ <globs> extends it instead), or set - to always run the suite
qa already runs test, lint and typecheck side by side under this default; set off to run them one after another
sweep warns on active locks older than 4 hours
no end-to-end command runs on the integrate branch; only test/lint/typecheck/build gate it
board events and gates reach nothing outside the terminal you happen to be watching
a fresh worktree installs no dependencies, so the first verify: on a real repo fails
a Builder that runs build: is rejected for dirtying tracked build output it does not own
seal merges and pushes the base locally; pr pushes only integrate/<date> and prints a PR URL
end: code reaches origin once, when finish closes the run (default with claim: local-lock); wave: every seal pushes base and its tag in one push (default with claim: claim-branch)
how many heavy jobs (verify lists, qa, the express suite, the push) run at once on this machine; 0 = no limit
speed --plan compares a plan's projected time with this; over it, the planner re-cuts once
a lone small task takes the express lane; off spends the full pipeline on everything
where seal writes the per-sprint report and polaris report regenerates it
nothing proves a task green — the wave gate, qa and CI all have no suite to run
no lint gate runs before a task reaches review
no type gate runs before a task reaches review
no build gate runs before a task reaches review
at most 5 Builder panes open themselves; the printed kickoffs stay uncapped

a second session waits 10 minutes for the integration lane before it gives up — NEVER raise past 10: the wait polls in the foreground, so 10 minutes is already the harness's 600s tool cap and a bigger bound makes the tool call return nothing and lose the whole wait; the long-wait fix is detaching (bg run + chunked bg wait --max 300), never a bigger number
an integration lease held this long counts as crashed and may be stolen
a handoff lands its own task through the integration lease and the last lane out seals the wave; integrator restores the classic wait-for-an-integrator handoff
a task worktree counts as live for 15 minutes after its last beat; done/release/sweep never remove a live worktree
no capture step: pack prints no SEE YOUR WORK section and handoff never asks for a screenshot
this repo declares no visual surface, so shot: never runs and a visually broken page can ship green
{PORT} in shot:/serve: stays literal — parallel builders share one dev-server port
pack prints no way to start the app for a capture; builders improvise a server
a session hops into the role polaris next names at each board-proven boundary; off restores one task per session
the repo updates itself at session start when the board is quiet; off leaves today's notice only
captures stay local and vanish on a fresh clone: nothing committed, nothing to show anyone
the layout pass runs when it is due — at the end of a run, or right after a typed update; off never offers it

the seal runs the tests mapped to what a wave changed every time, and the whole test: at most once an hour for the rest, and only while cards of the run are still to build (0 = every seal, off = only at finish)
a background job killed past its budget is run once more before it ends timed out (bg wait exit 4); 0 never retries
an armed away run with no sign of work for 20 minutes is marked stalled, and the notify: hook fires once
an armed away run that stops with work left is sent back to its next step (three tries, then it is marked stalled); off lets it stop
an away run arms a pulse every 30 minutes, so a session that stopped anyway is woken to carry on
only this same session re-enters an away run; desktop lets a POLARIS re-entry: prompt carry the approved plan into a new desktop session
an approved away run stays armed for 12 hours; after that the pulse and the away hooks treat it as over
a stopped away run is re-entered at most 3 times, then it parks for you
a long wait in a session with no background wake-up is handed to the kit's small job runner; off waits in chunked foreground calls (bg wait --max 540)
the job runner waits on Haiku, the cheapest model, and runs nothing but bg wait/status/tail; sonnet or inherit to change it (Opus and Fable are refused)
a project without POLARIS asks once, at the first request that would change it, whether to set it up; auto sets it up without asking for your own projects (see owners), off never mentions it
no account counts as yours, so auto_setup: auto only sets up projects with no origin remote; name the accounts that own your repos, comma-separated
